text:
The Maple Leafs lost 4-2 at home to Montreal on Saturday, and The Leafs Nation summed it up as Toronto continuing "to master the fake comeback." They are 8-8-2 and winless in four Atlantic Division games (0-3-1).

The record is generous. Toronto takes 46 percent of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and its shooters have scored 8.5 more goals than those chances predict. Our simulations give the Leafs a 13 percent playoff chance, which is a jarring number for a team with Auston Matthews, whose improved skating has made him a better playmaker than ever, per The Leafs Nation. Sergei Bobrovsky hasn't helped: .862 and 4.7 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, 1-4-0.

The off-ice noise is about the rest of the league. Kucherov's trade request in Tampa has every Toronto outlet asking what it means for Matthews, and trade proposals keep naming Kirill Marchenko and Easton Cowan. Cowan is back on Matthews' line, which has outscored teams 7-2, and Gavin McKenna said he's "Not Too Butthurt About It" after being bumped off the top power-play unit. The Jake McCabe and Darren Raddysh pair, at 44 percent of the chances, is where we'd start fixing things.
headline: Toronto's record is flattering a team that's losing the ice
